newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hoogovens, Belgian UGB in 3.0 bln bfr steel project.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens, Belgian UGB in 3.0 bln bfr steel project.

text.p: Belgian steel firm Usines Gustave Boel (UGB) has developed a 'partnership project' with Dutch metals group Hoogovens, which involved injecting three billion Belgian francs of fresh cash into Boel.
The deal is dependent on a restructuring at privately-held Boel's La Louviere, Belgium, plant involving the loss of 694 jobs.
The project, announced at a works council meeting on Thursday, aims to ensure the viability of Boel's steel activities and to safeguard 1,300 jobs at La Louviere.
Boel management invited staff representatives to start immediate discussions on the restructuring.
A formal agreement between Hoogovens and UGB on the 50/50 venture to recapitalise Boel is due by the end of the month.
Hoogovens has said it is interested in Boel's rolling mills at La Louviere and Maubeuge in northern France. The two sides agreed crude steel production at La Louviere was uneconomical.
The Boel rolling mills will help Hoogovens overcome an imbalance between its crude steel output of some six million tonnes a year and its 4.3 million tonne rolling capacity.
A major hurdle to the venture was removed last week when Boel and Belgium's largest steel maker Cockerill Sambre said they had abandoned a possible partnership due to a lack of synergies.

Talks between the two took place within the framework of efforts to create a "Great Walloon Steel Industry," a regional government-inspired bid to preserve the steel industry in Belgium's southern region of Wallonia and the jobs it provides.
The efforts were centred around loss-making Forges de Clabecq.
The European Union indicated earlier this week it would definitively block a 1.5 billion franc rescue plan for Clabecq by Wallonia because this constituted inadmissible state aid.
The decision is a nail in the coffin of Clabecq, which analysts say, can now only survive after a thorough restructuring involving plant closures and capacity cuts, and hundreds of job losses.
